newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Wednesday were seen steady, possibly firmer, on continued light marketings, livestock dealers said.

Calls for possibly firmer prices were expressed by dealers in the eastern Corn Belt where IBP Inc has expanded slaughter at its Logansport, Ind., plant by adding a second shift on Monday as announced in March, they said.

Strong demand for hogs to fill the plant's second shift needs could firm Indiana and Illinois hog prices and at least partially offset potential weakness from slaughter cutbacks by other plants in the Midwest, several livestock dealers said.

Hog prices also could be underpinned Wednesday if pork prices turn higher as a result of this week's reduced slaughter, some sources noted. Pork prices at midday were mixed, with fresh hams steady-firm, pork bellies firm and lean trimmings $2.00 to $3.00 per cwt lower, but trade was slow, USDA reported. There were 15.0 loads of pork and 25.25 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold, USDA said.

Interior Iowa top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $56.00 to $56.50 per cwt and Illinois top prices were seen at $56.00, traders in those areas said. Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant could range $55.00 to $56.75.
